I would keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so this is the crop system I know best and the one I trust most for stable grain output, manageable labor, and lower market risk. At my age, I would not make the year more complicated by switching a big share of land into crops that need more careful marketing or hand labor. I would plant improved winter wheat because it is dependable and fits my soil and irrigation conditions, then follow it with hybrid summer maize because it gives strong yield after wheat harvest and makes full use of the season. I would manage fertilizer in a moderate way, not too light because I want steady yield, and not too heavy because that wastes money and can cause lodging. I would irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat here depends more on timely water, especially at jointing and grain filling. For maize, I would save time with no-tillage after wheat harvest, keep plant protection practical, and focus on weed and pest control at the key stages. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield, but to get a reliable harvest with work I can actually handle well.
